body:
Third pool session. 3h 15m runtime across six dives. The sub stayed dry.

Dive 1 and 2 were thruster-only runs, no autonomy enabled. We were characterizing the thrust response curve for each motor individually. The data showed a consistent 120ms lag between command and full output on all T200s, which is within the expected spec.

Dives 3 through 5 introduced the depth hold PID. First dive: the sub oscillated badly at 1.2m target depth. The integral term was wound up from the initial descent and took 8 seconds to decay. Reduced integral gain by 40% and added anti-windup on the integrator. Dive 4 was clean, settling to within 4cm of target depth in 2.3 seconds. Dive 5 repeated dive 4 twice with a deliberate disturbance (hand push) to test recovery. Recovery time was 1.1 seconds both times.

Dive 6 was cut short at 28 minutes. The camera housing fogged internally, likely from residual moisture trapped during assembly. Not a leak. We pulled the sub and packed it to dry overnight with desiccant.

Camera housing assembly protocol updated: mandatory 30-minute desiccant pre-soak before sealing. The fog cost us about 40 minutes of pool time, which was the last 40 minutes of our reservation.

Next session is scheduled for May 15. Plan: heading hold PID and the first attempt at combined depth-plus-heading autonomy.
